name: application-language-switcher
title: Language Switcher
description: Language/locale switcher list with a flag, label, and checkmark on the active locale, driven by real selection state.
useWhen: The product supports multiple languages/locales and users need an explicit way to switch between them.
You want each locale represented with both a flag and a written label, not the flag alone (flags are not reliable language indicators on their own).
The active locale should be clearly marked so users can confirm which is currently selected.
avoidWhen: The product only supports one language — there is nothing to switch between.
You need a full settings row with more locale metadata (date format, currency) — pair this list inside a larger `profile-edit-form` section instead of using it standalone.
Locale should be inferred automatically with no manual override — a switcher implies user choice; don't add one for a locked locale.
responsiveBehavior: Fixed-width popover-style panel; anchor it to a trigger button (e.g. the current locale name in a footer or header) and let your popover/positioning layer handle placement.
accessibility: The list has role="listbox" with an aria-label describing it as Language, and each row is role="option" with aria-selected reflecting the active locale.
Flags are decorative (aria-hidden) since the written language name is the accessible label, not the emoji flag.
The active locale carries both a bold label and an explicit checkmark icon, not color alone, to indicate selection.
Each option is a real button, keyboard focusable and operable without a pointer.

variants.title: Language Switcher
variants.description: Five locales with English (US) active, each row showing a flag and label.
accessibility: Selecting a locale updates real aria-selected state and the checkmark together, so they can never disagree.

variants.title: Language Switcher (Dark)
variants.description: Language switcher adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Active-row text and checkmark colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
